![](asset:P000563-stem-1)Figure shows two blocks in contact sliding down an inclined surface of inclination 37°. The friction coefficient between the block A of mass 2.0 kg and the incline is μ<sub>1</sub>, and that between the block B of mass 4.0 kg and the incline is μ<sub>2</sub>. Calculate the acceleration of the 2.0 kg block if
(i) μ<sub>1</sub> = 0.20 and μ<sub>2</sub> = 0.30,
(ii) μ<sub>1</sub> = 0.30 and μ<sub>2</sub> = 0.20.

assets.alt: Two blocks touching on a 37° incline: A, 2 kg, lower down with coefficient μ₁, and B, 4 kg, above it with μ₂.
Blocks A and B on a 37° incline, with A alone accelerating at g(0.6 − 0.8μ). Notes: (i) A faster (4.4 vs 3.6), they separate; (ii) B faster, B pushes A, common a = 4.13 m/s².
